Now researchers at the Department of Energy's [SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory](https://www6.slac.stanford.edu/) and collaborators have captured an exquisitely detailed, step-by-step look at copper atoms as they underwent extreme thermal heating. Published in [*Nature Communications*](<https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-75970-1 >), the results revealed a key parameter that allowed copper's crystal lattice to melt steadily, rather than collapse instantaneously as earlier simulations predicte

“These results greatly improve the simulations we use to predict which materials have the best shot at surviving the extreme conditions of future fusion reaction chambers,” said [Mianzhen Mo](https://heds.slac.stanford.edu/person/mianzhen-mo), a SLAC staff scientist who led the research. “They also demonstrate the incredible, atomic-scale resolution imaging we can achieve at SLAC’s electron camera.”

Researchers use computer simulations, aided by [AI and machine learning](https://www6.slac.stanford.edu/topics/ai-and-machine-learning), to sift through innumerable combinations of elements and identify promising candidate materials for real-world testing. In recent years, Mo’s group has investigated the properties of [tungsten](https://www6.slac.stanford.edu/news/2024-03-13-new-research-tungsten-unlocks-potential-improving-fusion-materials) after it was flagged as a potential material for fusio

Researchers use computer simulations, aided by [AI and machine learning](https://www6.slac.stanford.edu/topics/ai-and-machine-learning), to sift through innumerable combinations of elements and identify promising candidate materials for real-world testing. In recent years, Mo’s group has investigated the properties of [tungsten](https://www6.slac.stanford.edu/news/2024-03-13-new-research-tungsten-unlocks-potential-improving-fusion-materials) after it was flagged as a potential material for fusio

The team brought their sample to [MeV-UED](https://lcls.slac.stanford.edu/instruments/mev-ued), SLAC's powerful electron camera that captures atomic and molecular movements down to the femtosecond – millionths of a billionth of a second. They blasted a thin copper film with laser heat, then sent an electron beam to image the sample as it heated. What they saw surprised them.

“This is a major improvement to modeling capabilities and their predictive power going forward,” said Siegfried Glenzer, [High Energy Density Science](https://heds.slac.stanford.edu/) division director, professor for photon science at SLAC and senior author on the paper. “The precision and resolution with which we are able to see these things demonstrates how remarkable this technique is at unveiling these ultrafast, ultrasmall dynamics.”

This research is supported in part by the DOE Office of Science Fusion Energy Sciences and SLAC’s [Laboratory Directed Research & Development Program](https://ldrd.slac.stanford.edu/). LCLS is a DOE Office of Science user facility.

source_links.context: NVIDIA has released [Nemotron 3 Diarization](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization), an open-weight speaker diarization model on Hugging Face. It answers one question about any conversation: who spoke when. The 100M-parameter model tracks up to 8 speakers, including when voices overlap. One checkpoint handles both offline recordings and real-time streaming.

**Is it deployable?** Yes. The weights are released under the [OpenMDW License 1.1](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/), which permits commercial use. It runs on Linux through NVIDIA NeMo, using Ampere, Ada Lovelace, Hopper, or Blackwell GPUs.

NVIDIA’s earlier [Streaming Sortformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18446) checkpoint, `diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2.1`, supported 4 speakers. Nemotron 3 Diarization doubles that limit to 8. According to [NVIDIA’s announcement](https://x.com/NVIDIAAI/status/2102775666366435450), the target is messy multi-party audio where people talk at once.

NVIDIA’s earlier [Streaming Sortformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18446) checkpoint, `diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2.1`, supported 4 speakers. Nemotron 3 Diarization doubles that limit to 8. According to [NVIDIA’s announcement](https://x.com/NVIDIAAI/status/2102775666366435450), the target is messy multi-party audio where people talk at once.

The model follows the [Sortformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.06656) approach of ordering speakers by arrival time. The first new voice takes channel 1, the next takes channel 2, and so on. This keeps labels stable across streaming chunks, so the model does not have to re-match speakers to channels for every chunk.

Input-buffer latency equals (chunk + right context) × 80 ms. The table uses DIHARD III full-set DER and batch-32 compiled throughput from the [model card](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Diarization).

Training combined about 10,000 hours of real conversations with 82,611 hours of simulated multi-talker mixtures. The mix included real-world multi-speaker audio licensed from [David AI](https://www.withdavid.ai/). Adding the David AI data cut compound DER from 11.19% to 10.42%. The licensed source audio for the simulated mixtures spans 21 languages.
**Install [NVIDIA NeMo Speech](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech) with Python 3.12 or later:**

from nemo.collections.asr.models import SortformerEncLabelModel

diar_model.eval()
segments = diar_model.diarize(audio=["conversation.wav"], batch_size=1)
```

source_links.context: Voice input on phones has been solved for years. What has not been solved is the output. Speak into most dictation tools and you get back exactly what you said, fillers and false starts included, in a note you then have to clean up and move somewhere else. [SpeakON](https://speakon.sjv.io/Gbd2EL) attacks that gap with hardware: a 25 g magnetic button that snaps to the back of an iPhone, carries its own microphone, and writes finished text straight into whatever app is already open.

[SpeakON](https://speakon.sjv.io/Gbd2EL) calls the category an AI Communicator, and takes its framing from the Communicator in Star Trek: you should not need to be at a terminal to stay connected. The target user is a founder, manager, consultant or field professional who is not short on ideas but is short on the time to stop, unlock a phone, switch apps and type.

The [SpeakON device](https://speakon.sjv.io/Gbd2EL) measures 58 x 58 x 6 mm and weighs 25 g. A 220 mAh cell is rated for 10 or more hours of continuous use and more than 2 weeks of standby, charging in under 1.5 hours over USB-C. It carries 128 MB of onboard storage, a stated capture range of roughly 60 cm, and supports up to 5 minutes of continuous input per press. The box includes a USB-C cable and a magnetic ring for iPhones without MagSafe.

[SpeakON](https://speakon.sjv.io/Gbd2EL) installs as a system-wide iOS keyboard extension. That is the mechanism that lets output appear inside Messages, Mail, Slack, Notion or any field that accepts keyboard input, with no app switching and no clipboard round trip. Press, speak, and the processed text appears directly in the active text field, ready for review or editing before you send it. The app requires iOS 16.0 or above; magnetic attachment requires iPhone 12 or newer.

[SpeakON](https://speakon.sjv.io/Gbd2EL) states that voice data is encrypted, never sold and not used to train AI models, with user control over cloud sync. The company reports SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA compliance, and GDPR compliance.

The device sells for $129 one time in the United States, with Pro Lifetime included and no recurring fee. Colorways are Pearl, Black, Navy Blue, Amber and Sage. Shipping covers the 48 contiguous states plus Washington, D.C., with a 30-day return window and a 12-month warranty. The [companion app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/speakon-ai-voice-keyboard/id6757388240) is a free download and works without the hardware, which is the cheapest way to evaluate the text-shaping layer before buying the bu

Looking ahead, [SpeakON Agent](https://speakon.sjv.io/Gbd2EL), which extends the same press from producing text to preparing reviewable Notes, Tasks and user-confirmed Actions, becomes available in October, 2026.

source_links.context: [IT之家](https://www.ithome.com/) 8 月 9 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，记者从国家发展改革委了解到，今年以来，我国算力底座进一步夯实，首个全国产 10 万卡人工智能超集群日前正式投用。标志着我国算力基础设施建设迈入 10 万卡级部署新阶段。

source_links.anchor: 中国首个全国产 10 万卡 AI 超集群“曙光 8000（登峰）”正式落成
source_links.context: IT之家注意到，中科曙光今年 7 月宣布，[中国首个全国产 10 万卡 AI 超集群“曙光 8000（登峰）”正式落成](https://www.ithome.com/0/974/966.htm)，并接入国家超算互联网。曙光 8000（登峰）采用“超智融合”技术路线，面向高精度科学计算与低精度智能计算的复合需求，支持 FP64 到 INT8 全精度，可覆盖科学计算、大模型训练、AI 推理、工业仿真等场景。
7 月 17 日，IT之家前往 2026 世界人工智能大会现场，[拍到了“曙光 8000（登峰）”真机](https://www.ithome.com/0/978/037.htm)。这套系统采用浸没式相变液冷技术，可支撑单机柜 MW 级高功率密度部署，并通过国产冷媒、全年自然冷却等方式提升集群能效。

source_links.context: AI can already solve long-horizon MirrorCode tasks, despite their difficulty. For example, Claude Opus 4.7 reimplemented gotree: a bioinformatics toolkit with ~16,000 lines of Go and 40+ commands.<sup>[1](https://epoch.ai#user-content-fn-1)</sup> We believe this same task would take a human engineer without AI assistance 2–17 weeks. Opus 4.7 solved it in 14 hours, costing $251.

One important caveat to these results is data contamination. Because MirrorCode tasks involve reimplementing open-source programs, AI models are likely to have seen the original codebases in pretraining. This might lead to inflated performance on the benchmark. However, AI successfully reimplemented several target programs that passed our memorization screen, and failed to reimplement programs where the screen showed evidence of memorization. This suggests that the results were not dominated by

MirrorCode is not fully solved. For our regularly updated leaderboard, we report **MirrorCode (ML, +Private, 2L)**. This means we run the 15 target programs from the Medium and Large buckets, and drop the Small bucket. Each target program is evaluated in two implementation languages (generally Go and Ada) giving 30 tasks. We run each task three times, with a budget of 10 billion tokens and 7 days per attempt, using high reasoning effort where the API supports it.[2](https://epoch.ai#user-content

We release our scaffold and 22 of the 25 MirrorCode target programs (totaling 132 task instances across the six supported programming languages) as [open-source](https://github.com/epoch-research/MirrorCode), with the other three targets held out as a private test set.

reader_metadata.description: Scientific discovery is driven by scientists generating hypotheses for complex problems that undergo rigorous experimental validation. To augment this process, we introduce Co-Scientist, a multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) system built on Gemini for structured scientific thinking and hypothesis generation. Co-Scientist aims to help scientists discover new original knowledge. Conditioned on their research objectives and previous scientific evidence, it formulates demonstrably novel research hypotheses for experimental verification. The system’s design involves agents continuously generating, critiquing and refining hypotheses accelerated by scaling test-time compute. Key contributions include (1) a multi-agent architecture with an asynchronous task execution framework for flexible compute scaling, and (2) a tournament evolution process for self-improving hypotheses generation. Automated evaluations show continued benefits of test-time compute scaling, improving hypothesis quality over time. Although this is a general-purpose system, we focus the validation in three biomedical applications: drug repurposing; novel-target discovery1; and explaining mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance2. Specifically, Co-Scientist helped to identify new drug-repurposing candidates and synergistic combination therapies for acute myeloid leukaemia that were validated through in vitro experiments. These real-world validations demonstrate the potential of Co-Scientist to accelerate scientific discovery and usher in an era of AI-empowered scientists.
reader_metadata.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist

source_links.context: On Monday, OpenAI announced a new independent advisory group hosted at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, New Jersey. Called the [Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence](https://openai.com/index/advisory-group-on-mathematics-and-ai/), the group is meant to give mathematicians more input into the company’s math-oriented research.

source_links.anchor: a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem
source_links.context: The announcement comes after the abrupt publication of [a solution to the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/08/openai-fought-dirty-on-career-making-math-problem-says-nyu-mathematician/). As part of the announcement of the new group, OpenAI also claims that the same internal model has resolved more than 100 additional open problems across most areas of mathematics.

Many prominent mathematicians have taken issue with the frenzied pace of those results. Earlier this month, 25 Fields Medal-winning mathematicians signed [an open letter](https://mathandai.org/) arguing that AI labs are threatening their intellectual work as they seek to one-up each other with solutions to famous math problems.

The Institute for Advanced Study emphasized this point in its own announcement. “Although we will give advice, we do not have decision making power at any AI company, and the responsibility for the decisions made by any company will rest with that company,” [said](https://agmai.org) the institute in a press release.
